ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a light green circle with a green boundary; a pink line segment extends from one side boundary of the circle to the other side boundary and passes through the black center point inside the circle; beside the segment is labeled “222 m”. The problem asks to find the area of the circle and round to the nearest tenth. Reasoning: Because this pink segment passes through the center and has both endpoints on the circle, it represents the diameter of the circle, d = 222 m. The radius is half the diameter, so r = 222 / 2 = 111 m. The area formula of a circle is A = πr², so A = π × 111² = π × 12321 ≈ 38707.563. Rounded to the nearest tenth is 38707.6.
